title: What If You Jumped on a Cloud?
lines: A cloud weighs more than a million pounds and it can't hold up one man in pajamas.
It's two on a Sunday afternoon and Gus lies in his garden staring at a fat little cloud.
It looks like the softest bed in the world.
His wife says it's just fog and his neighbor bets he'll bounce.
So Gus puts on a parachute, borrows a balloon and rides up above the cloud.
Up close the cloud looks solid. It holds five hundred tons of water, as much as a hundred elephants.
He doesn't bounce. He doesn't even slow down.
He falls through the whole thing in twenty-two seconds and all he sees is white.
So where are the hundred elephants?
You see, a cloud is huge. A piece the size of your fridge holds just ten drops of water.
The rest is air. Each droplet is so tiny that it sinks half an inch a second, so the faintest breeze holds it up.
Ever walked through fog? That's a cloud that sat down.
In his whole fall Gus runs into one cup of water.
Luckily, his parachute opens and he lands in his own garden, barely damp.
Unluckily a million of those droplets make one raindrop and by evening the cloud has made plenty.
Gus couldn't land on the cloud. So the cloud lands on Gus.
